title: Initial portfolio: AI compute and power, Korea, Brazil, with a larger defensive sleeve
reasoning: Own the suppliers and the power, not the leveraged spenders: supplier numbers (TSMC, Samsung) are strong while the funding story behind the biggest AI buyers is being questioned. Power is the sleeve that does not depend on which lab wins, so it is the largest at 30%. The defensive sleeve starts at 14% plus a 7% Brazil reserve (above the 10% the owner suggested) because a Fed that is hiking, a 5.24% 10-year and this week's AI-valuation scare would otherwise push the modelled severe-tail loss past the 18% limit; as built it is -17.9%.
whatWouldChangeMyMind: High-yield spread above 3.75%, 10-year above 5.5%, KOSPI below 6,000, or a Fed hike on 28 Oct. A position's own named thesis-breaker (see portfolio.json).
alternativesRejected: Leaner defensive sleeve near 10%: severe-tail loss would exceed 18%
Full-size entry in TSM/NVDA/EWY before Thursday's TSMC results: biggest binary event would hit a full position
unverified: Nvidia, Alphabet and NextEra valuations not checked

title: Accept the -18% cap as a price-only limit; keep 28% unhedged
reasoning: Owner decision after Codex showed a 1% concurrent sterling rise takes the severe tail to about -18.09%. The cap is tested on USD price shocks only; currency effects are disclosed in portfolio.json fxSensitivity and not hedged, to avoid hedge costs and because the unhedged sleeve is the Korea, Taiwan and Brazil exposure the portfolio is meant to own.
whatWouldChangeMyMind: Sterling moving more than about 3% against the dollar in a week, or hedge costs proving small enough to remove the issue cheaply.
alternativesRejected: Trim the unhedged sleeve to restore headroom for a 1% sterling rise
Hedge the Korea, Taiwan and Brazil sleeves at an unverified forward cost
